newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW sees earnings outpacing sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: VW sees earnings outpacing sales in 1997.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG, painting a bright outlook for its future, said on Thursday it expected 1997 profits to outpace sales growth despite slender prospects for global economic growth that would likely limit demand for new vehicles.

VW said in its 1996 annual report that it expected "postive results" for 1997 despite forecasts for slow consumer spending as many European nations slash spending to qualify for European monetary union set to begin in 1999.
"We expect our 1997 earnings to grow overproportionally to sales growth," VW chief financial officer Bruno Adelt said in the text of a speech at the carmaker's annual news conference.
VW chief executive Ferdinand Piech was more cautious, telling the conference that "a continuation of the current economic conditions would lead us to expect positive developments for the year".

The German carmaker's forecast comes after it reported earlier this year a near doubling in 1996 group profit to 678 million marks ($393.5 million) from 336 million marks in 1995 behind a 10.6 percent growth in sales to 3.977 billion marks and a 10 percent growth in group vehicle sales to nearly four million units.

VW, Europe's largest carmaker, said in the report that it expected the German economy to be aided by exports but to show limited growth and little improvement in the nagging jobless crisis that would likely dampen sales.
Slower sales growth in Germany and western Europe, however, should be compensated by higher growth rates in Asia and Latin America, the carmaker said.

"In consideration of these factors, the vehicle industry can expect a small increase in global vehicle demand. We expect positive impulses from markets in Asia, Latin America, as well as in Middle and Eastern Europe," VW said in the report.
But the carmaker noted, "For western Europe and Germany, we are expecting a small increase in demand."
